title: Blood Pressure Measurement Using Kent Coda 8 Tail-Cuff Method
author: Deborah A. Howatt
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.iygcftw

steps.title: Set warming platform temperature
steps.instruction: Turn on the warming platform and select a temperature level (Level 1 = 32 °C, Level 2 = 35 °C, Level 3 = 38 °C). The ideal range for blood‑pressure analysis is 33–35 °C. Verify tail temperature with an infrared thermometer; avoid tails that are too cold or a platform that is too hot (stress, dehydration, death).

steps.title: Choose appropriate animal holder
steps.instruction: Select the holder size that matches the mouse weight: Small for 10–25 g, Medium for 25–50 g, Large for 50–100 g.

steps.title: Power on Coda 8 system
steps.instruction: Turn on the Coda 8 blood‑pressure system and the computer, then open the Coda 8 program (v3 icon).

steps.title: Test cuffs without mice
steps.instruction: Run a “TEST RUN” with no mice, select all channels with the test ID, and execute a couple of cycles. The red (O‑cuff) and blue (VPR‑cuff) lines on each graph must intersect. If they do not, replace the offending cuff and repeat the test until intersection occurs.

steps.title: Load mouse and attach cuffs
steps.instruction: Gently pick up the mouse by the tail, place it into the appropriately sized holder, thread the tail first through the O‑cuff then the VPR‑cuff, secure the hoses in the holder notch, and adjust the O‑cuff so it is neither too tight nor too loose. Position the holder on the designated warming‑platform channel and rotate mice daily across channels to detect channel‑specific issues.

substeps.instruction: Pick up mouse by tail and place into holder
Thread tail through O‑cuff then VPR‑cuff
Slide hose into holder notch to secure cuffs
Adjust O‑cuff tightness appropriately
Place holder on assigned platform channel
Rotate mice each day (e.g., day 1: mouse 1→channel 1, mouse 2→channel 2; day 2: mouse 1→channel 2, etc.)

steps.title: Acclimate mice in holders
steps.instruction: Leave mice in the holders with cuffs on for at least 5 minutes before measurement. Cover tails with a blanket if the environment is noisy or temperature is low. Do not measure mice with wounded, short, severely dermatitis‑affected, very sick, or overly irritated tails.

steps.title: Configure experiment in software
steps.instruction: In Device Manager select Coda 8 – Channels 1‑8, choose “Use these devices”, then File → New. Choose “Experiment” (enter study name) or “Session” (enter session name). Enter experiment name, select researcher, click Next. Enter session name, set cycles to 20 (acclimation cycle = 0), click Next. In Specimen pool, add new mice via Manage specimens and move mouse numbers to the active area, click Next. Set cuff deflation time to 20 seconds, click Next through remaining screens, and press “Finish” to start measurements.

substeps.instruction: Select Coda 8 – Channels 1‑8
Select “Use these devices”
File → New
Choose “Experiment” (enter study name) or “Session” (enter session name)
Enter experiment name and select researcher → Next
Enter session name, set cycles = 20 (acclimation = 0) → Next
Manage specimens: add mice, move to active area → Next
Set cuff deflation time to 20 seconds → Next
Proceed through remaining configuration screens → Finish

steps.title: Run measurement and monitor
steps.instruction: During the run do not touch the mice and stay in the room. If a mouse pulls its tail free, pause the run and re‑thread the tail. Observe that the red line slopes downward and the blue line slopes upward until they intersect; lack of intersection indicates cuff leakage—pause and replace the leaking cuff. A full 20‑cycle run takes approximately 15 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Do not touch mice; remain present
If tail frees, pause and re‑thread
Watch red line (O‑cuff) decline and blue line (VPR‑cuff) rise to intersect
If lines do not intersect, replace leaking cuff
Note that 20 cycles ≈ 15 min

steps.title: Release mice after run
steps.instruction: Immediately after the run finishes, release the mice from the holders and return them to their cages before performing any other actions.

steps.title: Clean equipment between runs
steps.instruction: Clean mouse holders and the warming platform with baby wipes, removing all blood, feces, and urine. Do not use Clidox, as it degrades cuffs and plastic components.

steps.title: Record and validate BP data
steps.instruction: Collect at least 5 accepted systolic BP readings per mouse per day. Ensure the standard deviation is ≤30 mmHg and each systolic value is >50 mmHg. Review the graphs of each accepted run to confirm reliability.
